eventMetadata.context_description: Oklahoma City Thunder's 50.5% implied probability as 2026 NBA Champion stems from their status as the Western Conference top seed with a league-best 64-18 regular-season record and defending champions, capped by a dominant 119-84 Game 1 rout of the No. 8 Suns on April 19, where Shai Gilgeous-Alexander orchestrated 25 points and seven assists amid team depth. San Antonio Spurs at 11.6% reflect their No. 2 West positioning (62-20) and Victor Wembanyama's impact, despite splitting first-round games with Portland. Boston Celtics' 12.1% holds on No. 2 East seed strength (56-26) and playoff pedigree, even after a 1-1 series tie versus Philadelphia. Denver Nuggets (8.5%) and Cleveland Cavaliers (5.1%) benefit from Nikola Jokić's triple-double dominance and Donovan Mitchell's form in early playoff wins, though West paths remain grueling amid no major injuries altering rosters. Trader consensus favors OKC's clearest title runway.

eventMetadata.context_description: Keldon Johnson's official announcement as the 2025-26 Kia NBA Sixth Man of the Year on April 22 has locked in Polymarket trader consensus at 100% implied probability, mirroring the league's verdict after he dominated off the bench in all 82 regular-season games for the San Antonio Spurs. Setting a franchise record with 1,081 bench points—second league-wide in scoring and rebounds from reserves—he fueled the Spurs' 62-win campaign, outpacing finalists Tim Hardaway Jr. and Jaime Jaquez Jr. in efficiency and impact, the first such honor for San Antonio since Manu Ginóbili in 2008. Absent an extraordinary NBA reversal, no realistic scenarios challenge this resolution.

title: New WNBA CBA agreement by...?
description:
This market will resolve according to the date on which the WNBA and WNBA players association sign a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA). The listed market will resolve to "Yes" if the date of signing is between market creation and the listed date 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the listed market will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, a CBA is considered ‘executed’ only when the final written agreement has been formally signed by authorized representatives of both the WNBA and the WNBA Players Association. Tentative agreements, ratifications, or agreements pending signature do not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

title: Will the NBA alter draft lottery rules?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the NBA Board of Governors passes any vote that changes the rules of the NBA Draft Lottery before the start of the 2026 NBA Draft, scheduled for June 24, 2026, regardless of when the changes take effect. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Changes to the Draft Lottery may include rules related, but not limited to: the number of teams in the lottery, the percentages for picks allotted to teams in the lottery, etc. Changes related to date, location, or other logistical changes will not be considered.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ongoing anti-tanking reform discussions have traders pricing a 55% implied probability on the NBA altering draft lottery rules, reflecting closely contested sentiment amid strong ownership and NBPA support for flattening odds to curb incentive distortions. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver voiced enthusiasm for overhauls on April 9, following the league's March 27 unveiling of three major proposals, including equal 8% No. 1 pick chances for the bottom 10 non-playoff teams, building on 2019 changes that failed to fully deter tanking by squads like the Wizards, Nets, and Pacers—now holding top 14% lottery odds after recent tiebreakers. While no final Board of Governors vote has occurred, widespread tanking in the 2025-26 standings underscores urgency ahead of the May lottery.

title: 2026 Euroleague: Winner
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed club wins the 2025-2026 Euroleague season. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed participant to win the 2025-2026 Euroleague per the rules of the Euroleague (e.g., participant is eliminated), the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If multiple teams are declared winners, this market will resolve in favor of the team whose listed name comes first alphabetically.

If this event is cancelled, postponed after May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or a champion has not been declared within this timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source will be official information from the Euroleague (https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/); however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Olympiacos Piraeus tops trader consensus at 35% implied probability after clinching the No. 1 regular-season seed with a 26-12 record and top-rated offense (123.0 ORTG), securing home-court advantage through the quarterfinals and potential Final Four path against the No. 8 play-in winner. Fenerbahçe Beko (27%) follows as the No. 4 seed, boosted by snapping a late slide in Round 38 to draw Zalgiris Kaunas, leveraging their home edge in best-of-five series. Real Madrid's third-place finish (19.5%) positions them favorably versus sixth-seed Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv, the surprise debutants with strong wins including over Panathinaikos. Hapoel's 18% reflects upset potential from their sixth-place surge, while Panathinaikos (15.5%) faces play-in uncertainty against Valencia or Monaco amid recent losses. Recent Round 38 results solidified the playoff bracket starting April 28, emphasizing seeding and form in this tightly contested race.

eventMetadata.context_description: All four contenders—La Laguna Tenerife, Unicaja, Rytas Vilnius, and AEK BC—advanced to the 2025-26 Basketball Champions League Final Four in Badalona after grinding best-of-3 quarterfinal series concluding April 15, fueling the razor-thin trader consensus around 48-49% implied probabilities. Defending champions Unicaja swept Alba Berlin 2-0 with clutch wins (72-69, 88-85), leveraging their perfect 6-0 regular season group record; AEK BC overcame Joventut Badalona 2-1 (87-84, 66-88, 72-67) behind RaiQuan Gray and Frank Bartley's award-winning play; Rytas Vilnius dispatched ERA Nymburk 2-0 (77-70, 70-69) on dominant defense; and Tenerife rallied past Galatasaray 2-1 (84-83, 62-64, 99-59), powered by Giorgi Shermadini's quarterfinals MVP dominance. With May 7 semifinals pitting Rytas vs. Tenerife and Unicaja vs. AEK in single-elimination format, balanced depth, recent momentum, and head-to-head uncertainties keep the race intensely competitive.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus in the Liga Nacional de Básquetbol winner market clusters tightly around 48-49% for frontrunners La Unión de Formosa, Regatas Corrientes, Ferro Carril Oeste, Racing de Chivilcoy, San Martín de Corrientes, Oberá Tennis Club, Obras Basket, and Platense, reflecting playoff volatility just nine days after the 12-team field locked in on April 13. Regular-season parity defined the race, with Quimsa and Gimnasia y Esgrima de Comodoro Rivadavia tying atop at 24-12, but contenders like Regatas (23-13, 8-2 L10) and Oberá (23-13, 7-3 L10) carry hot streaks into best-of-five quarterfinals. Weekend openers delivered drama—Regatas' 93-69 rout of Argentino, Peñarol's 87-80 edge over Ferro—highlighting defensive grinds and upset risks that sustain the bunched odds amid uncertain series outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Los Angeles Lakers shares at 56.5% implied probability for LeBron James' next team in 2026-27 free agency, reflecting his current tenure, son Bronny's presence, and reports that the Lakers remain open to re-signing despite a potential roster pivot around new addition Luka Dončić. Elevated Spurs odds (33.4%) stem from speculation pairing James with Victor Wembanyama for veteran mentorship on a cap-rich rebuild, while Grizzlies (31.9%) and Trail Blazers (24.6%) draw bets as flexible suitors despite James' recent backlash-inducing criticism of Memphis hotels and suggestion the franchise relocate to Nashville. Cavaliers linger at 17% on lingering homecoming buzz, with retirement still viable per April 17 updates indicating no firm plans.

title: NBA Playoffs: Team to advance to Conference Semifinals
description:
This market will resolve “Yes” if the listed team advances to the Conference Semifinals of the 2026 NBA Playoffs. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for the listed team to reach the Conference Semifinals of the 2026 NBA Playoffs (e.g. they are eliminated), the associated market will resolve to "No".

If the 2026 NBA Playoffs are cancelled, postponed after June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET or the results of the 2026 Playoffs first round have not been declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA (https://www.nba.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the 2026 NBA playoffs first round underway, trader consensus favors Oklahoma City Thunder to emerge from a favorable Western Conference bracket after their dominant 119-84 Game 1 rout of Phoenix Suns, positioning them for an easier path amid series tied 1-1 elsewhere including Spurs-Blazers (Victor Wembanyama in concussion protocol) and Nuggets-Timberwolves. In the East, Cleveland Cavaliers' 2-0 lead over Toronto Raptors strengthens their contender status, while Boston Celtics and New York Knicks hold steady in tied series against 76ers and Hawks respectively; however, Orlando Magic's stunning 1-0 upset over top seed Detroit Pistons introduces volatility. Short-handed Lakers lead Houston Rockets 2-0 despite Luka Doncic out and Kevin Durant questionable, with Game 2s today potentially shifting momentum ahead of conference semifinals.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus reflects a tightly contested Eastern Conference Finals MVP market, with Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Maxey, and Jaylen Brown clustered at 24-25% implied probabilities amid first-round volatility. Orlando's 112-101 Game 1 upset over top-seeded Detroit—despite Cade Cunningham's playoff career-high 39 points—exposed Pistons' supporting cast issues but preserved his 20.5% standing on regular-season dominance and home-court edge. Philadelphia's 111-97 Game 2 rout of Boston to tie the series 1-1 boosted Maxey after a poor Game 1, matching Tatum and Brown's output from the Celtics' 123-91 opener. Knicks' 113-102 win behind Jalen Brunson's 28 points and Cavaliers' 126-113 victory led by Donovan Mitchell's 32 keep multiple stars viable, as no ECF path clarifies yet.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at a dominant 72% implied probability for Western Conference Finals MVP, reflecting the Oklahoma City Thunder's position as the No. 1 seed (64-18 regular season) and heavy favorites (68% on related markets) to advance through the playoffs after a strong Game 1 win in the first round versus Phoenix. Shai's MVP-caliber campaign—32.7 PPG, 6.4 APG, elite defense—plus his reigning Finals MVP status from last year, has traders betting on his carry job amid OKC's rest advantage and depth. Anthony Edwards (26.6%) trails as Minnesota's playoff star in a competitive bracket, while Jamal Murray (17.2%) and Luka Doncic (14.8%) draw support from Denver and Dallas' veteran cores, though OKC's opening-week momentum shifted lines sharply in their favor.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers hold a commanding 2-0 series lead over the Toronto Raptors in their Eastern Conference first-round matchup after dominant home wins—126-113 in Game 1 and 115-105 in Game 2—fueled by Donovan Mitchell's 30+ point outbursts in both and James Harden's playmaking. The Cavaliers' superior regular-season record (52-30 vs. 46-36) and home-court advantage underscore trader consensus favoring an Under 5.5 resolution at 66.5% implied probability, as Cleveland eyes a quick closeout. Toronto's offense has sputtered without starting guard Immanuel Quickley (hamstring, out for Games 1-2), while backup center Thomas Bryant remains sidelined for the Cavs but minimally impacts their depth. Game 3 shifts to Toronto, yet Raptors' recent playoff struggles and backcourt vulnerabilities suggest limited comeback potential absent major adjustments.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Knicks-Hawks first-round playoff series stands tied 1-1 after Atlanta's stunning 107-106 Game 2 comeback at Madison Square Garden, where CJ McCollum erupted for 32 points and the Hawks overcame a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit, exposing New York's late-game collapse despite Jalen Brunson's 29 points. This razor-thin margin, following New York's 113-102 Game 1 rout led by Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, underscores a competitive matchup shifting to Atlanta for Game 3 with Hawks' home-court edge in Games 3-4-5. Atlanta's thin frontcourt—Jock Landale out with a high-ankle sprain, Onyeka Okongwu battling knee inflammation—tests their depth against a healthier Knicks roster featuring probable OG Anunoby, fueling trader consensus at 64% implied probability for over 5.5 total games as both squads demonstrate resilience in tight spots.

Lakers maintain home-court advantage for Game 2, with LeBron's heavy minutes and recent momentum from a seven-game regular-season win streak against Houston underscoring trader focus on LA's depth amid ongoing injury challenges.

eventMetadata.context_description: The New York Knicks and Atlanta Hawks head into Game 3 of their first-round NBA playoffs series tied 1-1, with Atlanta hosting at State Farm Arena after a thrilling 107-106 Game 2 comeback win on April 20, where CJ McCollum erupted for 32 points to erase a 12-point fourth-quarter deficit. Knicks coach Mike Brown's lineup decisions drew scrutiny in the collapse, despite Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns combining for strong Game 1 outputs of 28 and 19 points. Hawks' Jock Landale remains out with a right ankle sprain, but Onyeka Okongwu played through knee inflammation in Game 2; Knicks report no major injuries, with OG Anunoby probable after a Game 1 ankle tweak. Home-court edge and Hawks' momentum from McCollum and Jalen Johnson fuel trader focus on a competitive battle.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers lead the Toronto Raptors 2-0 in their Eastern Conference first-round playoff series following commanding home wins—126-113 in Game 1 and 115-105 in Game 2—powered by Donovan Mitchell's 30+ scoring outbursts, James Harden's 28 points and assists in Game 2, Evan Mobley's 25 points, and Jarrett Allen's interior presence. Game 3 shifts to Toronto on April 23, offering the Raptors home-court advantage and desperation to stave off a 3-0 hole amid their 22 turnovers and subpar three-point shooting in Game 2. Toronto's Immanuel Quickley sat out with a hamstring sprain, while Cleveland's Thomas Bryant remains out (calf); no major new injuries reported, but Raptors' urgency and crowd support could test Cavs' road form in this closely watched matchup.

title: Which team will Steve Kerr join next by the end of 2026?
description:

Roles taken in addition to an existing primary role (such as a national team or advisory appointment held concurrently with a club role) do not qualify. Only his sole or primary basketball role counts for resolution.

Interim, temporary, or short-term appointments do not count, provided they are officially announced as such.

If Steve Kerr officially announces his retirement from basketball, or if no qualifying announcement has been made by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution sources will be official announcements from Steve Kerr and/or the acquiring team. A consensus of credible reporting may be used where official announcements are ambiguous or delayed.

eventMetadata.context_description: In Game 2 of their first-round Eastern Conference playoff series, the No. 8 Orlando Magic hold a 1-0 lead after a 112-101 road upset over the No. 1 Detroit Pistons in Game 1 on April 19, fueled by Paolo Banchero's 23 points and Orlando's stout defense limiting Detroit's supporting cast despite Cade Cunningham's 39-point effort. Detroit, boasting a dominant 60-22 regular-season record and home-court advantage at Little Caesars Arena, aims to even the series with their high-powered offense and rebounding edge. Magic forward Jonathan Isaac remains sidelined by a left knee sprain that's hampered him since March, thinning their frontcourt depth, while Wendell Carter Jr. plays with a protective face mask post-nasal fracture; Pistons report no major injuries. Recent head-to-heads favor Detroit historically, but Orlando's momentum, rest advantage from fewer regular-season minutes, and defensive versatility could prolong this competitive matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: Oklahoma City Thunder's dominant 119-84 Game 1 rout over the Phoenix Suns in the 2026 NBA Western Conference first-round playoffs, fueled by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 25 points and stifling defense, has solidified trader consensus favoring the top-seeded defending champions ahead of Game 2 at Paycom Center. The Suns, the No. 8 play-in seed with a 45-37 regular-season record, enter with mounting injury concerns: Grayson Allen (left hamstring strain), Jordan Goodwin (left calf soreness from Game 1), and Mark Williams (left foot soreness) all listed questionable per the latest injury report. Thunder roster remains largely healthy, leveraging home-court advantage and momentum from their 64-18 campaign, while Phoenix must adjust rotations amid depth issues and a quick turnaround.

eventMetadata.context_description: Lakers hold a 2-0 lead in their Western Conference first-round playoff series after narrow home wins over the Rockets—107-98 in Game 1 and 101-94 in Game 2—despite the absences of Luka Doncic (left hamstring strain, out indefinitely) and Austin Reaves (left oblique strain), with LeBron James delivering 28 points, eight rebounds, and seven assists in the latest victory. Heading to Game 3 on Friday at Toyota Center, Houston gains home-court advantage and desperation to avoid a 3-0 hole, missing Fred VanVleet (right knee ACL repair) and Steven Adams (ankle surgery) but boasting depth led by Kevin Durant, whose knee contusion status remains key. Traders weigh Lakers' road fatigue and roster depletion against Rockets' rebound potential in this pivotal matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Portland Trail Blazers stunned the San Antonio Spurs 106-103 in Game 2 on April 21, evening their first-round Western Conference playoff series at 1-1 after Victor Wembanyama exited early in the second quarter due to a confirmed concussion from a hard fall, putting his Game 3 availability in serious doubt—Spurs went 12-6 without him during the regular season. Scoot Henderson erupted for 31 points to lead Portland's 16-4 closing run, compensating for Damian Lillard's season-ending Achilles injury. Game 3 shifts to Portland on April 24, giving the 42-40 seventh seed home-court edge against the 62-20 second-seeded Spurs, whose depth faces a critical test amid the closely contested matchup.
